newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco papers OK'd for secondhand-smoke trial.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco papers OK'd for secondhand-smoke trial.

text.p: A Florida appeals court rejected a tobacco-industry request that 16 confidential Brown & Williamson Tobacco Co. documents be kept out of a landmark secondhand smoke trial, an official said Tuesday.

The ruling by the 3rd Florida District Court of Appeal comes amid jury selection for the Broin case, in which some 60,000 flight attendants are claiming $5 billion in damages for injuries allegedly caused by passengers cigarette smoke aboard U.S. airlines.
The appeals court upheld the ruling of trial Judge Robert Kaye, who said plaintiff attorneys may use 16 of 28 documents during the Broin trial. He kept 12 documents out of the trial.

Attorneys for Brown & Williamson, a unit of B.A.T Industries of Britain, had argued that while almost all of the documents were widely available in books and elsewhere, they were still covered by client-attorney privilege and should not be used against tobacco companies during a trial.
